references.text: God promised Abraham that he would go to his fathers in peace and be buried at a good old age—a prophecy fulfilled here.
Isaac's death is described with similar language: he breathed his last, died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days.
Jacob's death is described with almost identical wording: he drew his feet up into the bed, breathed his last, and was gathered to his people.
A wisdom saying about reaching the grave in mature age, like a sheaf of grain harvested in its time—a parallel to Abraham's peaceful death.
David died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor—the same expression used for Abraham's death.
The Letter to the Hebrews notes that the patriarchs of faith, including Abraham, died in faith without having received what was promised, but saw it and greeted it from afar.
Ishmael's death with the same wording as Abraham's confirms that God's blessing and belonging also apply to those who are not heirs of the messianic promise.
